headline: A city dressed as its game, cookies adults cannot buy and a break hidden in code

worked.text: One big game release, worked from both ends: dress the real city it is set in, or serve the players too young for it.
A rule or habit becomes the trigger: an age check turns into the reward, an equals sign turns into a break.
Each shows up where people already are: landmarks they already photograph, a coding tool they already use.

picked.text: Every piece was a landmark: a giant sign lowered onto an arena, 10 new murals and a themed NBA game night.
It flips the age check: the pack is for players too young for the game, with bouncers set to check ID.
The break hides inside the work: equals signs in AI-written code count up to a break and a voucher.

adapt: Look at who a big cultural moment leaves out, then make something only they can get.
Find a rule or gate your audience knows and flip it, so the usual outsiders are the ones let in.
Pick a symbol or action people repeat all day and make it the trigger for your brand moment.
Dress a few real places properly, with local partners who gain from the attention, instead of many scattered placements.
Deliver a small utility inside a tool people already use, so there is nothing new to install.

campaigns.summary: A real city was dressed as the game world set in it, from an arena rooftop sign to new murals and an NBA team's themed game night.
campaigns.did: Before Grand Theft Auto VI came out on 19 November, Rockstar dressed the real Miami as the game's Vice City. A helicopter lowered a giant pink "Welcome to Vice City" sign onto the Miami Heat's arena and a deal with Wynwood Walls brought 10 new murals made for the game. On the eve of release the Heat played the Bucks in Vice City uniforms on a custom court.
campaigns.why: The game is set in a version of a real city, so the city became the media. Each piece is a landmark people already photograph. Adweek, citing Sensor Tower, put preorders past $1.5 billion the day before release, and Sports Illustrated, citing ESPN, says game-night gear sold out within 90 minutes.
campaigns.steal: Find the place where your product's world already exists and dress it, with local partners who gain from the attention. A few landmarks done properly beat many scattered placements.

campaigns.summary: A limited-edition cookie pack for gamers too young for the 18+ game GTA VI, with a QR code that opens a private Discord community.
campaigns.did: ChipsMore! made 18 Unrestricted, a limited-edition cookie pack for gamers too young for the 18+ game GTA VI. A QR code behind the label opens a private Discord community where Malaysian gaming personalities are set to share tips for games such as Mobile Legends: Bang Bang and PUBG Mobile. The packs are to be sold at booths in Lotus's stores, where bouncers will check MyKad identity documents.
campaigns.why: Most brands chased the adults playing on launch day. This one picked the audience left out and turned the age check, usually a barrier, into the reward. No results are out yet, and ContentGrip notes that any effect on store traffic is unreported.
campaigns.steal: Look at who a big cultural moment excludes and build something only they can get. Reversing a familiar gate, so the usual outsiders are the ones let in, gives people a story to retell.

campaigns.summary: A prompt for AI coding assistants counts every equals sign a developer generates and prompts a break once enough pile up.
campaigns.did: Developers copy a prompt from a microsite into their AI coding assistant. It runs alongside the session and counts the equals signs in the code, since two parallel lines look like two KitKat fingers. At set thresholds a break reminder appears, and at the final one the developer gets a GrabMart voucher for KitKat.
campaigns.why: The insight is that fast AI code removes the natural pauses in a coder's day. The brand line arrives inside the work instead of beside it. B&T, Marketing-Interactive and WeRSM covered it; no results are out yet.
campaigns.steal: Find a symbol or action your audience repeats all day and make it trigger your brand moment. Deliver a small utility through a tool people already use, so there is nothing new to install.
